text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- ABN AMRO bank to restructure its German subsidiary for the second time this year. (p1)
- Three cities in eastern Netherlands jointly offer brewer Grolsch a range of business locations. (p1)
- Haarlem court defers Amsterdam Schiphol Airport's limitaions on night flights until Friday. (p1)
- Inflation in the Netherlands rises 2.4 pct in July, the highest level so far this year. (p5)
- Realty fund Wereldhave upgrades this year's earnings per share forecast to 8.20 guilders from 7.90. (p15)
- Ton Risseuw, chief of Automation company Getronics, has no plans to leave yet. (p2)
- Lovers Rail, rival to Dutch Railways NS is angry over NS conducting passenger count in its trains. (p3)
- Tour operators adding ten percent excess charges on holidays because of high dollar. (p3)
- Supermarket chain Edah sees turnover grow after introducing an electronic payments card. (p11)
- Iraq places Royal Dutch/Shell on the black list of oil companies. (p11).
- Retailer Ahold plans to save millions of guilders by taking on board the implementation of unemployment and disability benefit schemes. (p3)
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert seeks to use tax windfall for improving spending power of people on minimum wages. (p1)
